guesses.reason: Dense short-to-medium gray coat with a white muzzle, chest, and inverted-V blaze between the eyes is the classic random-bred bicolor pattern.
Slightly longer, wispy fur tufting from the ears and along the cheeks hints at a medium-length coat.
Large, tall, upright ears with feathery ear furnishings and a fine-boned wedge-ish face show faint Angora-type traits.

breed.appearance: A gray-and-white bicolor cat with a solid slate-blue-gray cap, ears, and back, and a crisp white inverted-V blaze that runs up from the muzzle to a narrow point between the ears, flowing into a white muzzle, chin, chest, and front legs. Large, tall, pointed ears with pinkish inner skin and wispy pale tufts frame a moderately wedge-shaped face with round golden-amber eyes, a soft pink nose with a darker rose tip, and long white whiskers. The coat is short to medium and plush, with a slight dark smudge of gray at the inner corners of the eyes along the edges of the blaze.
breed.fun_fact: Gray-and-white bicolor cats like Gaia are famous for their striking 'masked' faces, and every one has a blaze pattern that's completely unique!
